courseLedger.name: Personal & Professional Development
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
courseLedger.contribution: MandatoryYear1PPD; does not establish aerospace subject coverage.
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Introduction to Programming
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Introduces computational problem-solving and programming in Python. Students develop structured programs using branching, iteration, functions and data collections, then progress to recursion, exception handling and object-oriented programming with inheritance. Elements of logic, sets and enumeration support computational reasoning. Exercises and projects require students to write, trace, test, debug and explain programs that solve problems of moderate complexity.
courseLedger.contribution: supplies programming, testing and debugging for mathematical models and autonomous-system software
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Sustainability Essentials I
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Uses planetary boundaries to introduce scientific tools for understanding sustainability and human impacts on Earth systems. Students interpret graphs and uncertainty, build simple dynamic models, and learn chemical, thermodynamic and mechanical principles relevant to environmental processes. Topics connect climate, ocean acidification, nutrient cycles, energy and materials. An iterative laboratory project makes starch-based biopolymers and measures their strength and elasticity to improve the formulation.
courseLedger.contribution: establishes documented physics, chemistry, materials, mathematics and modelling foundations for sustainability technologies
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Consumer Product Design
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Teaches consumer-product design and development through projects that progress from understanding an existing product to creating a new one. Students investigate product mechanisms and environmental impact, interview potential customers, translate needs into specifications, select concepts, and develop production plans and prototypes where feasible. The final project integrates these stages with industrial scaling and elementary economic analysis. Sustainability, including material use, repairability, lifespan and circularity, informs design decisions throughout.
courseLedger.contribution: Complementary engineering-design practice: product mechanisms, user needs, specifications, concept selection, production planning and prototypes where feasible; no guaranteed fabrication, quantitative structural model or aircraft project is assumed.
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Mathematical Methods
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Develops single-variable calculus and related mathematical tools for modelling scientific problems. Functions, limits and differentiation lead to optimization, Taylor series, complex numbers, integration and differential equations. Students solve problems analytically and with Mathematica, including numerical approximation. A project implements, analyzes and adapts a dynamic model, requiring interpretation of its behaviour and explanation of the computational results.
courseLedger.contribution: Direct mathematical foundation: single-variable calculus, complex numbers and differential-equation modelling, with analytical and Mathematica work. Matrix/eigenvalue study belongs to the separate Linear Algebra course and is not attributed here.
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Sustainability Essentials II
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Connects wave physics, chemistry and materials science to sustainability questions. Students study wave behaviour and observation methods, chemical analysis, microscopic material structure and macroscopic stress and strain. Practical sessions include wave applications and chemistry laboratory work. Reflective inquiries and a final project critically assess sustainability campaigns, identify greenwashing and communicate evidence-based improvements to a public audience.
courseLedger.contribution: Complementary physical/material inquiry: mechanical/electromagnetic waves, spectroscopy, material structure, stress/strain and laboratory analysis in sustainability settings; no aerospace-structure design is claimed.
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Optimization Methods in AI
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Studies search and optimization for rational agents in known, complex and adversarial environments. Students move from uninformed and heuristic search to local and global optimization, first- and second-order methods and population approaches. Adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimization extend the toolkit. Laboratories and projects require algorithm tracing, implementation and evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.
courseLedger.contribution: implements search, global and local optimisation and constraint satisfaction for complex systems
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Image Processing & Computer Vision
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Examines how digital images are represented, processed and interpreted to recognize structures and objects. Spatial and spectral representations, colour and image statistics support filtering, segmentation, curve and feature detection, tracking and object classification. Students use Python and OpenCV to implement image-processing techniques, investigate spectral representations, and build a recognition pipeline whose performance is benchmarked on previously unseen images.
courseLedger.contribution: studies image and video processing, feature detection and tracking relevant to automated observation without claiming physical instrumentation
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Develops life-cycle approaches to evaluating products, processes and services within a circular economy. Students examine environmental, social and health consequences from resource extraction to disposal or reuse, together with costs, revenues and management strategies. Three preliminary projects develop different parts or forms of life-cycle analysis, followed by a project that integrates the stages into a full product or process assessment.
courseLedger.contribution: Actual life-cycle evaluation of products/processes,not aircraft design.
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Introduction to Data Science
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Introduces data analysis and visualization in R through practical work with tabular, textual and spatial data. Students import, clean, transform and join data, explore patterns, and construct visualizations using tidy-data principles and the grammar of graphics. Web scraping and basic programming functions extend the workflow. A student research project applies these tools to a question using data from a field of interest.
courseLedger.contribution: Complementary general data preparation, transformation and visualisation inRwith a research project; aerospace or sensor datasets are not guaranteed.
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Algorithms & Data Structures
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Studies algorithm design and analysis, emphasizing how algorithms and data structures affect execution time. Students examine sorting, searching, random-number generation, string matching and graph algorithms, then study computability, verification, reductions and complexity classes. Programming and mathematical exercises develop algorithmic understanding, while projects require students to design, execute and report experimental investigations of performance.
courseLedger.contribution: develops algorithms and data structures with performance analysis for efficient technical computation
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Linear Algebra
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Develops linear algebra from systems of equations and matrix operations to vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues and orthogonality. Students study least-squares approximation, symmetric matrices, quadratic forms and singular value decomposition. Applications include discrete signals, difference equations, Markov chains, dynamical systems, graphics and principal component analysis. Mathematica exercises teach computer-algebra approaches to larger problems alongside analytical problem-solving.
courseLedger.contribution: develops vector spaces, matrices and linear transformations for coupled-system models
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Earth Observation
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Develops geospatial analysis for investigating environmental change and designing responses to Earth-system problems. Hands-on ArcGIS Pro work covers spatial data models, georeferencing, projections, visualization, queries, transformations and surface analysis. Remote-sensing foundations extend into spectral signatures, acquisition systems, preprocessing and image processing. A collaborative case study applies geospatial methods to an environmental research question.
courseLedger.contribution: Actual GIS and remote-sensing acquisition/data analysis for environmental study,not satellite engineering.
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Computational & Numerical Methods
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Develops numerical solutions to mathematical problems that lack convenient analytical solutions, emphasizing when algorithms work and how to validate their output. Students study numerical root finding, interpolation, differentiation, quadrature, ordinary differential equations, and linear and nonlinear systems. Mathematica notebooks apply and compare textbook algorithms with built-in routines, with attention to roundoff, convergence, error, stability and sensitivity.
courseLedger.contribution: implements stable numerical methods for equations, interpolation, integration and differential equations
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Linear Systems
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Analyzes continuous- and discrete-time signals and linear time-invariant systems through differential or difference equations, impulse responses and frequency-domain representations. Convolution, Fourier series and transforms lead into sampling and reconstruction, filtering, communication systems, Laplace and Z-transforms, and linear feedback. Mathematica laboratories and an applied project connect mathematical properties to signal processing and system behaviour.
courseLedger.contribution: Direct systems-method connection: continuous/discrete signals, differential or difference equations, Fourier/Laplace/Z-transforms, filtering, sampling and linear feedback; aerospace vehicle dynamics and a state-space syllabus are not assumed.
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Robotics
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Studies computational problems in robot motion and manipulation, supported by linear algebra, calculus and geometric modelling. Students analyze forward and inverse kinematics, configuration spaces, collision-free motion planning and grasping, with shorter introductions to sensing and control. Practical work programs a robot arm and gripper; research investigates inverse kinematics for an articulated structure. A smaller component examines a chosen legal, ethical, safety or human-robot issue.
courseLedger.contribution: studies robot kinematics, motion planning, collision avoidance and manipulation as computational autonomy rather than aircraft dynamics
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Probability & Statistics
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Provides a rigorous introduction to probability and mathematical statistics, from probability spaces and random variables to multivariate distributions and statistical inference. Students study estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and maximum-likelihood methods, followed by an introduction to Bayesian reasoning. Mathematica simulations verify analytical results. A substantial project implements and compares random-sampling algorithms, including inverse sampling, accept-reject sampling and Gibbs sampling.
courseLedger.contribution: develops probability, estimation and simulation for uncertain measurements and model parameters
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Machine Learning
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Introduces statistical learning for understanding data and predicting outcomes. Students study regression and classification, model accuracy, resampling, regularization, nonlinear models, trees, support vector machines and unsupervised learning. Practical assignments evaluate methods on real data using R or Python. Projects emphasize informative predictor construction, test-set prediction, appropriate model choice and clear reporting of results and limitations.
courseLedger.contribution: implements regression and statistical-learning methods relevant to prediction and operational data
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Decision-making in AI
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Develops the mathematical foundations of intelligent-agent decisions under uncertainty. Probability and Bayesian networks support belief updating and inference, while temporal models address changing environments. Decision theory, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems connect uncertainty to policies and expected utility. Multi-agent decisions introduce strategic and collective interaction, and probabilistic programming provides a framework for expressing models. Students work through equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.
courseLedger.contribution: Direct decision-method connection: probabilistic inference, Bayesian and temporal models, decision theory, partially observed policies and multi-agent interaction; no taught aircraft operations or resource-allocation project is assumed.
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Energy & Sustainability
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Studies renewable-energy resources, conversion technologies and their integration into sustainable energy systems. Solar, wind, hydro, geothermal and biomass resources are evaluated through physical principles, resource availability and generation potential. Storage, electricity grids and demand management connect individual technologies to system reliability. Quantitative exercises, a Polysun workshop, short experiments and local mini-grid work develop the ability to assess energy options in practical environmental and economic contexts.
courseLedger.contribution: Actual renewable-resource/conversion,grid/storage and practical energy assessment,not turbine aerodynamics or propulsion.
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Advanced Calculus
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Extends elementary calculus to multiple dimensions and differential equations, including complex‑valued functions. Uses computer algebra software to deepen analytical skills for science and data analysis applications.
courseLedger.contribution: extends calculus to multiple dimensions, complex functions and differential equations for technological systems
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Develops neural-network theory and practical implementation in Python, Keras and TensorFlow. Students build and train simple networks before studying multilayer architectures, backpropagation, regularization and model evaluation. Later work applies deep learning to computer vision, time series and text, including transformers. Projects construct predictors for tabular data and investigate an independently chosen image- or text-based prediction problem, with experimental results reported in a paper.
courseLedger.contribution: develops neural-network and deep-learning models for advanced data and image analysis
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Reinforcement Learning
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Explores reinforcement learning. Covers theoretical frameworks and algorithms and requires students to implement algorithms and build agents using neural networks that learn through trial and error.
courseLedger.contribution: implements reinforcement-learning agents and neural-network methods for adaptive autonomous behaviour
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

courseLedger.name: Renewable System Design
courseLedger.evidenceRead: Teaches assessment of energy usage patterns and strategies for reducing consumption or transitioning to cleaner energy. Explores solar, wind and bioenergy solutions and includes technical and economic analysis; students deliver a report and presentation to a partner company.
courseLedger.contribution: technically and economically assesses energy demand and solar, wind and bioenergy system designs
courseLedger.targetScope: Genuine mathematical/systems/autonomy/design/energy contribution considered; no assumed aerospace-specific project or course equivalence.

additionalLeadsRead.name: Building with Nature
additionalLeadsRead.profileRead: Introduces approaches that combine human infrastructure with natural processes and ecosystem health, with particular attention to Zeeland and the history of water management on Walcheren. Students examine applications across sandy and muddy coasts, lowland lakes, rivers and estuaries, cities and ports. Projects investigate ecological connectivity and formulate a Building with Nature intervention; a practical wall-building project explores constructed structures.
additionalLeadsRead.methodsRead: Building with Nature case analysis; Ecological-corridor project analysis; Nature-based intervention design; Construction and testing of model walls
additionalLeadsRead.finding: Nature-based coastal/ecological infrastructure and model-wall construction are genuine design work. They do not teach aerodynamic vehicle flow,flightloads or propulsion integration.

additionalLeadsRead.name: Living with Water
additionalLeadsRead.profileRead: Examines how delta societies manage water risks and opportunities, using Zeeland as a central case. Physical and ecological challenges such as flooding, salinization, freshwater scarcity, subsidence and pollution are connected to infrastructure, history, governance, law and justice. Students evaluate engineered and nature-based responses, considering trade-offs and long-term consequences. Site-based inquiry and a project apply these concepts to context-sensitive adaptation in a delta region.
additionalLeadsRead.methodsRead: Site-based water-management case analysis; Comparative appraisal of engineered and nature-based solutions; Context-sensitive adaptation-strategy development
additionalLeadsRead.finding: Delta water risks,infrastructure/ecology/governance and adaptation appraisal do not establish a fluid-dynamics or aircraft-design sequence.

additionalLeadsRead.name: R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation
additionalLeadsRead.profileRead: Studies resource circularity through solar-panel recycling, metal recovery from electronic waste, and soil remediation using plants and mycelium. Theory and extensive laboratory work connect material composition and separation technologies to resource yields, environmental consequences and recycling constraints. Students develop leaching protocols, analyze metal concentrations and recovery, cultivate fungal networks, and use microscopy to characterize materials and mycelium growth.
additionalLeadsRead.methodsRead: Solar-panel dismantling and physical separation; Chemical leaching; Experimental-protocol design; ICP metal analysis; Electrochemical recovery; Scanning electron microscopy and EDS; Mycelium cultivation and growth characterization; Recovery-yield and resource-potential calculations
additionalLeadsRead.finding: Real chemical/physical separation,metal recovery and material microscopy support resource-circularity research; they do not supply lightweight load-bearing vehicle-structure design.

additionalLeadsRead.name: Soils & Aquifers
additionalLeadsRead.profileRead: Examines soils and shallow aquifers through soil science, environmental chemistry and applied geophysics. Soil formation, functions, quality and threats connect to texture, structure, composition, biological activity and salinization. Field sampling and laboratory investigations characterize soil properties and sediment-cell behaviour. Seismic, electrical-resistivity and electromagnetic surveys investigate physical and geophysical properties of soils and aquifers. Students document procedures and observations, process field data in Excel, interpret results and develop evidence-based field and laboratory reports.
additionalLeadsRead.methodsRead: Soil coring and field sampling; Visual soil-structure assessment (grass-VESS); Aggregate-stability, texture and sieve tests; Soil pH, moisture, organic-content and leaching analyses; Microscopy and SEM-EDS; Sample preparation for ICP/IC and interpretation of ICP results; Methylene-blue testing with spectrophotometry/titration; Seismic surveying; Electrical-resistivity and electromagnetic surveying; Field-data processing in Excel
additionalLeadsRead.finding: Real soil/material sampling and seismic/electrical/electromagnetic surveying are acknowledged. Their taught inquiry is soil/aquifer characterisation,not aerodynamic flow,vehicle dynamics or aerospace experimental verification.
